title: CVE-2023-46218: cookie mixed case PSL bypass
excerpt:
## Summary:
libcurl fails to normalize the `hostname` and `cookie_domain` parameters passed to `psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable` function. As a result a malicious site can set a super cookie if the victim requests the url with hostname with any upper case characters in the domain part of the hostname.

libpsl `psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable` documentation  https://rockdaboot.github.io/libpsl/libpsl-Public-Suffix-List-functions.html#psl-is-cookie-domain-acceptable says the following:
```
Use helper function psl_str_to_utf8lower() for normalization of hostname and cookie_domain .
```
This is not done correctly and hence domains with uppercase characters will bypass the PSL check. Note that curl itself will later ignore the cookie domain capitalization and will match even lowercase hostname with the stored supercookie's mixed case domain.

It's also worth noting that the request `Host` header will reveal the mixed case used, which will allow the attacker to prepare the correct `Set-Cookie` domain for the attack.

## Steps To Reproduce:
  1. `echo -ne "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nSet-Cookie: super=oops; domain=co.UK\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n" | nc -v -l -q 1 -p 8888`
  2. `curl -v -c c.txt --resolve test.co.uk:8888:testserverip http://test.co.UK:8888`
  3.  `nc -v -l -p 7777`
  4. `curl -v -b c.txt --resolve other.co.uk:7777:testserverip http://other.co.uk:7777`

Note that the `super` cookie is sent to the `other.com.uk` site. In fact it will be sent to any `.co.uk` hosts now.

The generated cookie file:
```
# Netscape HTTP Cookie File
# https://curl.se/docs/http-cookies.html
# This file was generated by libcurl! Edit at your own risk.

.co.UK	TRUE	/	FALSE	0	super	oops
```

## Impact

Bypassing supercookie protection.

summary: libcurl fails to normalize hostname and cookie_domain in psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable, allowing uppercase domains to bypass PSL checks and set supercookies.

claims.text: libcurl fails to normalize hostname and cookie_domain parameters passed to psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable
claims.reasoning: No curl source code was provided for the revision checked (0b6d9ac8d9e1). The deterministic checks only confirm that the symbols 'hostname', 'cookie_domain', and 'psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable' exist in the codebase, but do not show how they are used or whether normalization occurs before the call. Without the calling code, I cannot verify whether libcurl fails to normalize these parameters.
The location claim depends on the same missing code. The function 'psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable' exists per deterministic checks, but its implementation and call sites were not provided.

claims.text: malicious site can set a super cookie if the victim requests the url with hostname with any upper case characters in the domain part of the hostname
claims.reasoning: The trigger claim describes an attack path that depends on the missing normalization. Without seeing the code that calls psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable and handles the cookie domain, I cannot confirm or contradict the described bypass.
Impact claim depends on the validity of C1-C3. If the bypass exists, the impact (bypassing supercookie protection) would follow, but the root cause is not verifiable from provided materials.
